key_insight: DAWN enables much faster inference for diffusion-based LLMs by explicitly modeling token dependencies and using that information to run safe, aggressive parallel decoding without sacrificing generation quality.
problem_solved: Existing diffusion LLM inference treats positions as independent and therefore uses overly conservative parallel strategies; this wastes latency headroom because semantically coupled tokens cause quality degradation when decoded independently.
method: Extract cross-token dependency signals (e.g., attention/interaction metrics or learned dependency predictors) to build a lightweight dependency graph over positions.
Use the graph to form dependency-aware groups and an adaptive scheduling policy that parallelizes independent positions while sequentially refining tightly coupled ones.
Apply selective refinement steps and confidence/uncertainty checks so the model preserves output quality while reducing overall decoding iterations.
impact: DAWN unlocks practical speedups for diffusion LLMs, making their parallel-decoding advantages usable in latency-sensitive applications and large-scale deployment without trading off generation quality.

Algorithm flowchart: dependency extraction → grouping → adaptive scheduler → selective refinement (compact pipeline view).
paper_title: DAWN: Dependency-Aware Fast Inference for Diffusion LLMs
paper_authors: Lizhuo Luo, Zhuoran Shi, Jiajun Luo, Zhi Wang, Shen Ren
